minutes.headline: Board renewed earth removal permits two weeks and disciplined the Conservation chair; Unitil tree plan and solar PILOT discussed.
minutes.summary: The Select Board heard the fourth-quarter FY19 revenue report and debated how conservatively to estimate local receipts. It received an informational solar PILOT presentation, discussed the Unitil storm resiliency tree program, and reviewed the town manager evaluation process with labor counsel. It announced discipline for the Conservation Commission chair, renewed earth removal permits, and went into executive session on police union bargaining.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to renew all active earth removal permits for two weeks, until September 3, 2019.
The board announced the Conservation Commission chair will give a public apology at the next televised meeting and attend open meeting law training.
The finance director reported fourth-quarter FY19 collections slightly over estimates, and members debated estimating local receipts closer to actuals.
The finance director is to provide a ten-year history of local receipts against estimates, and the town manager is to ask about reviving the ad-hoc budget committee.
The board heard an informational solar PILOT draft for 190 Electric Avenue, and left the town manager evaluation process without resolution.

why_it_matters: Local receipts estimates set how much revenue the town counts on before the tax rate is set, so estimating closer to actuals would change how much is left over as free cash.
A solar PILOT is a fixed payment in place of ordinary property tax on a site, so its terms decide what that property contributes to the tax base over twenty years.
A revived budget committee would change how the Finance Committee, School Committee and Select Board coordinate before Town Meeting votes.
watch_next: The earth removal permits run only until September 3, 2019, so the board must act again by that date.
The ten-year local receipts history from the finance director and the chair's draft town manager evaluation policy are due back to the board.
